page: Microsoft Azure E32-16as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with constrained core counts to support memory-heavy software deployments with optimized licensing requirements. Powered by AMD EPYC 7763 processors clocked at 3.525 GHz, this virtual machine provisions 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an expansive 16 GB of memory per allocated vCPU. Local storage is provided through a bundled 550 GB solid-state drive.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-thread execution, highlighted by a stress-ng single-core score of 2707.19 that places it in the upper quartile of comparable instances. Multi-core compute performance measures solidly in the median tier, evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core result of 21642.12 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10162. Memory throughput demonstrates 51.28 GB/sec in large-block read testing and 30.24 GB/sec during write operations. Database-centric synthetic tests yield 6814.49 operations in PassMark, alongside 16.2 million Redis set operations per second.

Cost efficiency is heavily influenced by the instance's constrained vCPU topology. By isolating 16 active vCPUs while retaining the full 256 GB RAM footprint typically assigned to a 32-core chassis, the instance reduces per-core software licensing expenditures while providing substantial memory capacity. Tradeoffs include modest uncached memory bandwidth relative to larger multi-socket configurations and a lack of hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

The E32-16as_v4 is suited for memory-intensive workloads that require moderate core counts. Primary enterprise workloads include in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, enterprise resource planning backends, and moderate relational databases requiring large buffer pools without the overhead of paying for idle CPU cores.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-16as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for memory-bound applications requiring high memory-to-core ratios and reduced per-core licensing overhead. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, it supplies 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores alongside 256 GB of system memory, delivering 16 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources also include a bundled 550 GB local SSD and Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Benchmark testing highlights strong single-core compute performance within the top 25 percent, complemented by steady middle-tier multi-core compute, delivering 16.2 million Redis SET operations per second and 51.28 GB/sec large-block memory read bandwidth. Although lacking hardware accelerators, its resource balance optimizes database workloads, in-memory caching solutions, and enterprise analytics platforms constrained by CPU core licensing costs.
